bluesky.text:
My inbox receives the newsletters I’m subscribed to in batches. Same days, same hours. Everybody follows the “best time to send” advice.
The effect: I don’t read them. It’s too much.
And most of them write about the same things, because everybody scans what’s popular right now.

My previous Claude Skills were influenced by what others did for themselves.

The best practices from others didn't make much sense to me. The results were me... but not me.

I moved it local too — the Skill, the notes, the process, all on my own machine now.

There are things AI does so well that I don’t review them. I assume they’re okay. And I realized I don’t know how to do the task myself, and I keep not knowing if I don’t ask for instructions.

https://substack.com/profile/17146826-jose-antonio-morales/note/c-384402094

I can't yet picture a European local government justifying paying for Claude or ChatGPT, knowing those companies hold data — anonymized or not — that a foreign authority could leverage whenever it suited their interests.

https://substack.com/@joseantoniomorales/note/c-298957832

Spreadsheets are practical and powerful tools. The key is not to treat them as the final home of your organization's data.

Store data, not just files.
